subject: Fwd: Feature gating for tenant audit export - Finvera
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvera.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finvera Procurement <procurement@finvera.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We had an internal follow-up with Compliance and the auditor flagged two must-have capabilities before we can move to procurement: a tenant-scoped audit-export endpoint (so each of our business units can pull their own model invocation logs) and a 7-year tamper-evident retention policy for those exported logs.

High level:
- Go-live target: Jan 15, 2027 (we need this in our SOC submission)
- Expected initial throughput: ~40k tokens/day across 5 tenant-ids, spikes to 200k tokens/day during batch runs
- Security: export must be signed and encrypted in transit; storage can be S3 (Finvera-managed) but we need an attestable chain of custody
- Commercial: if this is supported, Procurement is asking for a 3-year commitment at ~$1.2M ARR (we have internal approval contingent on the feature)

I attached our RFP excerpt with compliance language and a diagram of our data flow (Finvera_RFP_audit_requirements.pdf, finvera_dataflow.drawio).

Can Redwood support a way to pin/segment audit exports per-tenant and guarantee retention? This is the gating item for the deal. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

—Laura Chen
VP Engineering, Finvera
laura.chen@finvera.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Marissa / Karthik / Rishi — forwarding a hard gating ask from Finvera (big logo, potential $1.2M ARR commit). Procurement says they cannot proceed without tenant-scoped audit exports and 7-year retention.

Asks:
1) Feasibility / rough eng estimate: can we deliver a short-term exception (customer-scoped S3 export + signed attestation) in ~2–4 weeks vs full product work (API endpoint + UI + retention rules) which would take longer?
2) Any compliance/legal blockers (signing, chain-of-custody, tamper-evidence) we need to raise now?

Proposed immediate next step: 3pm today quick sync (15–20m) to decide whether to proceed with an exception approach and what the acceptance criteria are. Finvera wants a written capability statement to include in their SOC packet by Dec 3.

Attachments: Finvera_RFP_audit_requirements.pdf, finvera_dataflow.drawio

Thanks — Rachel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Thanks for the context — looks like two separate asks that map to different effort + risk profiles. Quick thoughts: 

Questions for Finvera (if you can get answers before the sync):
- Exact retention semantics: immutable vs legal hold; are they asking Redwood to store for 7 years or do they want an export contractually kept by Finvera for 7 years?
- Expected daily export file size and object count (impacts retention costs and lifecycle policies)
- Do they require HSM-signed manifests or is envelope signing sufficient?

Options (trade-offs):
- Option Quick (2–4w): Tenant-scoped export to customer S3 bucket with signed manifest (we generate a manifest per export cycle, sign it with a known key, set S3 lifecycle per their policy). Pros: low product change, fast. Cons: customer-managed storage means less control for Redwood, auditing UI not available.
- Option Product (8–12w): Tenant-scoped pinned audit API + managed retention (Redwood stores encrypted logs with 7y TTL + audit UI + export endpoint). Pros: fully managed, auditable, product-grade. Cons: larger engineering + infra cost, ongoing unit cost.
- Option Hybrid: Do Quick as an exception + commit to Product work in H1 2027 with prioritized ticket; offer Finvera a commercial concession for being early adopter.

I'll bring a short set of acceptance criteria to the sync (signatures, manifests, retention proof, S3 bucket policies).

—Marissa
Director, Product Management
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Product POV: we can greenlight Option Quick as an exception if Legal and Infra sign off, with the following conditions:

Acceptance criteria for the exception (sales needs to capture in the SOW):
- Redwood will implement tenant-scoped export to Finvera-owned S3 buckets with signed manifests.
- Retention is enforced by Finvera for exported data; Redwood will provide verifiable export logs (timestamps, checksums, signatures) for 7 years.
- Feature behind a feature-flag/tenant opt-in; Redwood not responsible for long-term storage costs.
- We require a commercial commitment: minimum 12-month reserved capacity or $1M ARR equivalent to justify the one-off implementation + on-call.

Timeline estimate (subject to eng confirmation):
- Scoping + Security review: 2 business days
- Engineering implementation (small export job + signing + docs): 2–3 weeks with 2 engineers
- Canaries & security attestation: 1 week

Next steps for Sales: please secure Finvera agreement to the acceptance criteria above in writing (Procurement needs to include this in their SOW). If they accept, we can target delivery by ~Dec 22 for a limited canary.

I'll turn this into a short spec if we decide to proceed.

—Karthik
VP Product
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T14:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Confirming engineering estimate and a few caveats: 

Estimate: 2 backend engineers + 1 infra engineer -> ~3 weeks of work to deliver tenant-scoped S3 export with:
- per-tenant manifest generation + signing (we'll use existing signing key rotator)
- export job scheduler (daily/near-real-time as needed)
- exported manifest + checksum logging stored in our audit bucket (we will keep that metadata for 7 years)
- docs + runbook + security questionnaire answers

Caveats / risks:
- We will need Finvera to provision the S3 bucket and grant write ACLs and a bucket policy; for tamper evidence we need either an object lock policy or Finvera-managed retention — if Finvera insists on Redwood-managed 7y retention we need a separate cost + approval conversation.
- Support burden: this will be a customer-specific integration until we productize — tagging and cleanup are manual today. Recommend feature flag per-tenant.

If Sales confirms SOW language and the commitment threshold Karthik called out, infra will allocate the people. I can kick off scoping immediately.

—Rishi
Engineering Lead, Platform
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvera.com>
Cc: Finvera Procurement <procurement@finvera.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Feature gating for Model Audit Logs

Laura — quick update and proposed path forward:

We can move forward with a customer-scoped S3 export (Option Quick) as a deal exception. Summary:
- Redwood will implement tenant-scoped exports to Finvera's S3 buckets with signed manifests and checksum logs; Redwood will retain export metadata (manifests/checksums) for 7 years.
- Finvera to provision the destination buckets with the agreed bucket policy or object-lock settings; if Finvera wants Redwood to manage the 7-year storage we will need a separate commercial amendment.
- We will deliver a security attestation and runbook for your SOC packet by Dec 3 (what you asked for).

Conditions:
- An SOW addendum confirming the acceptance criteria above and a 12-month committed contract or $1M ARR equivalent.
- Access to the Finvera S3 bucket and relevant IAM role for writes.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to return a signed SOW addendum (can be a short attachment) by Dec 6.
2) Once signed, infra/eng will start scoping and target a canary by Dec 22.
3) We'll follow with product work in H1 2027 to fully productize the feature if both sides agree.

I'll set up a short call tomorrow to get the SOW language in place. Thanks all — Rachel
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
